EICMA 2026 • Here Are Some of the Serious and Obscure Brands That EICMA 2026 Had To Offer – Worth Knowing About
Jay Leno Drives a Backhoe Around LA, It Has an Engine That Hit 406 MPH
15 photos
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube
Jay Leno started out in LA behind the wheel of a JCB 3CX Hydrogen backhoe loader, the world's first commercially available hydrogen combustion vehicle of its kind. The zero-tailpipe-emission construction machine is powered by the same engine architecture that set the mind-blowing 406.320 mph world land speed record.
No, Jay Leno isn't roaming the streets of Los Angeles at 400 mph (643.738 kph) because the JCB backhoe he has taken for a spin will by no means come anywhere near that speed. So he is moving around in a 19,180-pound (8,700-kilogram) monster.
The vehicle takes up an entire lane, measuring 18 feet 5 inches (5.62 meters) from the front loader bucket to the folded rear digging arm, 7 feet 9 inches (2.35 meters) across the rear tires, and 11 feet 10 inches (3.61 meters) to the top of the folded rear boom when driving on the road.
Jay Leno is sitting in a one-seat cab with a roof that stands at roughly 10 feet (3.0 meters), plus the protective cap housing the three hydrogen cylinders. The twist is that JCB planted the modified versions of its exact digger engine into a custom streamliner, designed entirely by computer and with zero wind tunnel testing.
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube To transform an industrial construction engine into a powerplant capable of crossing the 400 mph barrier, JCB and Ricardo hand-built six race engines. While the engineers retained the crankshaft and basic block geometry, they came up with custom forged pistons, upgraded connecting rods, and a dry-sump lubrication system, specifically designed to keep oil flowing while the engine lies flat on its side.
On August 11, 2026, retired Royal Air Force pilot Andy Green drove the JCB Hydromax streamliner at the Bonneville Salt Flats in Utah. He achieved an FIA-confirmed two-way average of 406.320 mph (653.909 kph), after averaging 400.623 mph (644.740 kph) on the first run and 412.135 mph (663.267 kph) on the return. He smashed the previous combustion record of 185.5 mph (298.533 kph).
The 32-foot-long Hydromax was built by motorsport engineering firm Prodrive and powered by two production-based 4.8-liter JCB hydrogen internal combustion engines, adapted from JCB’s digger power plants.
While the commercial backhoe engine makes just 74 horsepower (75 metric horsepower) and 324 pound-feet (440 Newton meters) of torque, the engineering firm Ricardo upgraded the twin turbocharged engines to push out 800 horsepower and 1,300 pound-feet of torque each. That would be a combined 1,600 horsepower and 2,600 pound-feet of torque.
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube Simple mathematics shows that each engine delivers more than ten times the power and roughly four times the torque of the 74-horsepower production JCB 448 ABH2 backhoe engine on which it is based.
Rather than generating electricity like a fuel cell, JCB's engine burns hydrogen gas in a traditional piston-and-cylinder setup, emitting only water vapor and zero carbon dioxide. Approved for commercial sale in Europe in early 2025, the JCB 3CX Hydrogen delivers the exact same digging power, torque, and rapid refueling times as a conventional diesel backhoe.
To handle that massive torque at over 400 mph, the Hydromax actually used standard clutches pulled straight from a production JCB backhoe loader like the one that Jay Leno took for a spin in the City of the Angels.
The engine that powers it is the same one that powered the world’s fastest hydrogen car to 406 mph. Not similar! The same! Ryan Ballard, Engineering Director at JCB, who led the engineering team for the JCB Hydromax, tells the story of the backhoe and of the vehicle that broke the speed record .
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube He brought along Wing Commander Andy Green OBE, a retired British Royal Air Force fighter pilot and the only person in history to break the sound barrier on land. He hit a mind-blowing 763.035 mph (Mach 1.016) in 1997, and his record still stands today.
However, from inside the car, he never heard the thunder-like explosion created by an object travels through the air faster than the speed of sound. " Technically, I am the only person on the planet who never had the chance to hear the sonic boom, " Andy Green says.
Parked in Jay Leno's garage is the 32-foot, twin-engined hydrogen-powered land speed record streamliner built by JCB and driven by Andy Green. Sitting right next to it, carrying the same engine but looking worlds apart, is the JCB 3CX backhoe.
The model launched back in May 2026 to replace the traditional diesel engine with a zero-carbon hydrogen internal combustion engine, delivering the exact same digging, loading, and roading performance.
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube The massive, bright yellow vehicle that Leno took for a spin in Los Angeles stores hydrogen at 350 bar of pressure in three carbon-fiber-wrapped aluminum tanks, sitting inside a protective cap on the cab roof. Regulators step that pressure down to under 20 bar before feeding the engine.
Filling the tanks from a ground-level port takes roughly ten minutes. A full tank of hydrogen provides approximately six hours of continuous operation. While the backhoe is ready to work, the JCB Hydromax's racing days are over. So it will most likely find a place in a museum once it completes its U.S. tour.
